Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

classic adjective and noun

of lasting worth

also a classic, a classic film, a classic book, a true classic, timeless

classical

Hor. Ep. 2.1.39

vetus atque probus

old and good, of proven worth

Horace’s words for a poem that has stood the test of time, in his mockery of the rule that a book becomes a classic at a hundred years. Probus is good, sound, of proven quality, of coins and goods as of people (Lewis & Short: nummī probī, Plaut.).

Other words

  • classicus, classica, classicum — classic, of the first rank

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. classic: liber classicus (1726)

    Gellius’s word for a first-rank author (see classic, an author), stretched in modern Latin to any work of lasting worth.

  • nōbilis, nōbile — famous, well known

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. nōbilis

    For a work everybody knows (see famous).

Examples

  • est vetus atque probus, centum quī perficit annōs.

    he is old and good who reaches a hundred years.Hor. Ep. 2.1.39

See also classic, famous, old.

SourcesLewis & Short: probus · Lewis & Short: classicus · Lewis & Short: nobilis

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. classic.
